lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.focus: graphing half-planes as inequality solution sets
lessonRef.title: Unit assessment: graphing half-planes as inequality solution sets

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  -7x + 5y = 2
  -6x + 5y = 5
choices: exactly one solution
infinitely many solutions
no solution
exactly two solutions

items.prompt: Is the point (1, -3) in the solution region of -2x − 2y ≤ -2?
choices: No; substituting gives 4, which is greater than -2.
Yes; substituting gives 4 ≤ -2.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 2 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system is equivalent only when 2 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  4x + 1y = -1
  8x + 2y = 3
choices: infinitely many solutions
no solution
exactly one solution
exactly two solutions

items.prompt: Is the point (8, -6) in the solution region of 2x − 4y ≤ 1?
choices: Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
Yes; substituting gives 40 ≤ 1.
No; substituting gives 40, which is greater than 1.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 4 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system is equivalent only when 4 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  -4x − 5y = -7
  -3x − 5y = -4
choices: exactly two solutions
no solution
infinitely many solutions
exactly one solution
